correctness.rationale: The exact Newton coefficients of f(s)=q^((4-s)^2) give K as a sum of subset-incidence Gram matrices. Their signs establish PSD to the unique root of F, with strict PD before it. Inclusion incidence has rank C(n,3) at the root by an explicit column-independence induction. On J(8,4), two explicit pair-difference eigenvectors have eigenvalues F(q) and 1-2q+2q^9-q^16. F is strictly decreasing through q=13/25; the latter eigenvalue is negative from 13/25 to 1. Every J(n,4) contains the eight-point principal obstruction. Exact rational checker confirms the eigenvector and trace formulas, but does not substitute for these all-n arguments.

value.rationale: A natural Gaussian covariance based on the intrinsic graph distance of constant-weight binary observations has an exact uniform-in-n admissibility threshold, even though the Euclidean Gaussian is automatically admissible. The nontrivial boundary loses precisely the top harmonic rank, and a fixed eight-point witness proves that the threshold cannot be improved for any larger slice. A top-sector spectral revival at q=19/20 does not restore overall positivity, giving structural information beyond a simple sample computation. This answers a natural covariance design question on an infinite family of homogeneous finite spaces.
